dialogues.speaker: Abuzova
dialogues.text: Ugh... What shall we do? Isn't thre anyone who can help us out?

choices.text: What happened?

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Well, here's the thing. Lady Pavlina's organizing a wedding, and many Snegovik who don't usually visit the House of Hesperides are now flocking here from the four corners of the earth.

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: ...Ah. Sorry. I'm not saying that too many customers isn't a bad thing. It's good, naturally, but as you can see, we don't have enough seats for everyone.

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Two empty tables remain, but we have four guests...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Those who can enter the VIP room are all important people. There's a risk I might offend them if I arrange the seats willy-nilly... Ohh, what do I do?

choices.text: Why don't you leave it to me?

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Um, are you sure...? Actually, no, wait. You're a guest too, aren't you? Ohh, I'm going to get it from Aglaya if she hears I left my work to a guest, but...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: What do they say? Discretion's the better part of valor, and all that!

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Please, dear guest. I'm counting on you!

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: S—So here's the situation. The VIP Lounge currently has two tables remaining. One of them is in the main hall, and the other is in the side room.

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: The first guest... Um, actually, I don't remember his name. Let's just call him Guest 1.

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Guest 1 would like to rest in the side room, though he claims that the cracks in the walls there leave him ill at ease. Not that we can fix those now, though...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Guest 2 would like to have some alcohol in the main hall. She was measuring herself against another guest earlier, and wouldn't you know it? She drank them under the table without so much as going the slightest bit red...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Guest 3 and 4 are a pair of sisters from Novokitezhgrad.

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Guest 3 is fine sitting with anyone, but Guest 4 has stated that, "I shan't let my sister sit beside some brutish man. If she must do so, then I must be there as well!"

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: But it was this same guest who declared, "But goodness gracious, your tables here are so tiny, two people could barely sit down at one without elbowing each other!"

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: It does seem like Guest 4, that fussy little sister, will not accept sitting with any of the other two...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: And that's the situation. Honestly, I'm not sure how to go about this. So, could you discuss their preferred seating arrangements with them? I'll... take them to their seats later.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm... Let me give it a go, then...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Oh, thank you! You're such a lifesaver!

choices.text: Well, I'm sure you'll figure it out...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Oh dear... What should I do...

choices.text: Don't let me disturb you, then.

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: A—Alright, dear guest...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Abuzova follows your arrangement before asking the guests individually if they are pleased with it...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: It seems like everyone is content.

dialogues.speaker: Abuzova
dialogues.text: Phew... W—We made it!

dialogues.speaker: Abuzova
dialogues.text: Ohh, I can't thank you enough! If not for your help, I wouldn't have the foggiest how to do this. I'm just glad all the guests were satisfied...

choices.text: Friendly reminder, I'm a guest too...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Hehe, I wouldn't forget about you. Never!

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: This isn't much, but please take this as a reward for your help!

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: *sniffle* Oh, this is such a rarity — a guest who helps with problems rather than creates them! ... Well, um, this is not to say that the others were only making trouble...

choices.text: And what about my requests?

dialogues.speaker: Koshakva
dialogues.text: *sigh* Honestly... I could sit with just about anyone...

dialogues.speaker: Koshakva
dialogues.text: But my little sister, Khmelyova, <color=#00E1FFFF>will not let me sit alone with any man</color>. And where it is unavoidable, she insists on being there as well.

dialogues.speaker: Koshakva
dialogues.text: She's been like this since she was young, which is quite strange... But I suppose that's her way of being concerned for me.

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for her to rest in the side room...)

response.speaker: Koshakva
response.text: Alright... And now we're to wait for a staff member to guide us to our seat, yes? *sigh* I can only hope the arrangement is to Khmelyova's liking.

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for her to rest in the main hall...)

response.speaker: Koshakva
response.text: Alright... And now we're to wait for a staff member to guide us to our seat, yes? *sigh* I can only hope the arrangement is to Khmelyova's liking.

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: *sigh* ... Can no one... find any way to cover up the crack in that wall?

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: Seriously, don't the Snegurochka in this mansion realize just how frightening cracks are? Why, what if someone were to... s—see you through those cracks?

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: #Ah! The crack in the wall has been blocked, you say? Stupendous! You've a good heart, {M#Sir}{F#Ma'am}.

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for him to rest in the side room...)

response.speaker: Zlatov
response.text: I'll wait for a staff member to guide me to my seat. One sits where one is arranged to, and nowhere else. Worry not, I know the rules here in this mountain manor.

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for him to rest in the main hall...)

response.speaker: Zlatov
response.text: I'll wait for a staff member to guide me to my seat. One sits where one is arranged to, and nowhere else. Worry not, I know the rules here in this mountain manor.

dialogues.speaker: Isklynna
dialogues.text: Table requests? Heh, I've got none, save to <color=#00E1FFFF>sit in the main hall</color>. It's closer to the bar, you see.

dialogues.speaker: Isklynna
dialogues.text: I don't come to the House of Hesperides often. Might as well knock back a few extras while I'm at it, hmm? Hehe...

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for her to rest in the side room...)

response.speaker: Isklynna
response.text: Sure. I'll wait for the staff to arrive, then. Hmm. What shall I sample next...

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for her to rest in the main hall...)

response.speaker: Isklynna
response.text: Sure. I'll wait for the staff to arrive, then. Hmm. What shall I sample next...

dialogues.speaker: Hermeliva
dialogues.text: Hmph. I didn't realize the Duchess of the Snegurochka stocked her mansion with such tiny tables... This is an old-time fashion, so I hear...

dialogues.speaker: Hermeliva
dialogues.text: But we don't do "noble ladies making small talk around small tables" nowadays, do we? Goodness, two people would be starved of space sitting around these...

dialogues.speaker: Hermeliva
dialogues.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>And don't even think about making me share this with two other people</color>!

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for her to rest in the side room...)

response.speaker: Hermeliva
response.text: If the serving staff's work is not up to my expectations, the Snegovik in charge will be hearing from me, mark my words!

choices.text: (Alright. Let's arrange for her to rest in the main hall...)

response.speaker: Hermeliva
response.text: If the serving staff's work is not up to my expectations, the Snegovik in charge will be hearing from me, mark my words!

dialogues.text: Abuzova follows your arrangement before asking the guests individually if they are pleased with it...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But not everyone seems content...

dialogues.speaker: Abuzova
dialogues.text: Ugh, no, this still won't work...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me give this a bit more thought...

dialogues.speaker: Abuzova
dialogues.text: A—Alright then...

dialogues.speaker: Isklynna
dialogues.text: I don't come to the House of Hesperides often. Might as well knock back a few extras while I'm at it, hmm? Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Isklynna
dialogues.text: And then we'll see which fool shows up to challenge me to a drinking contest...

dialogues.speaker: Koshakva
dialogues.text: Sister, you don't really have to...

dialogues.speaker: Hermeliva
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm just worried about you... And really, how were we to know that Lady Pavlina's VIP Room could not even spare a single measly table?

dialogues.speaker: Hermeliva
dialogues.text: Besides, for you, my dear, purest sister, to sit next to a man... Oh, the very thought pierces me on every side...

dialogues.speaker: Koshakva
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Abuzova
dialogues.text: How has it gone, dear guest? Have you... figured the arrangement out, or do you need more time?

choices.text: We're good to go!

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Is that so? In that case, let me check in with them and see if they have any opinions on the matter...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Please wait here for the time being!

choices.text: I still need a little more time...

response.speaker: Abuzova
response.text: Alright. Do let me know once your arrangements are complete!

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: *sigh* Dear me, how did it come to this... *sigh* All I wanted was to repose in the side room for a while...

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: But look at that giant crack in the wall over there... How... How can one feel at peace with such a thing looming overhead?

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: And when I went to ask that Snegurochka, she said: "We're short-staffed and cannot repair it at present." Ah, but what if some voyeuristically-inspired soul were to glimpse me through that gap as I rest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can just block that crack, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: Block it, you say? Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Zlatov
dialogues.text: That... would just about do, yes. If we could indeed find something to block that crack, that would be lovely!
